entries.question: What is Tallyo?
entries.answer: Tallyo is a straightforward place to manage your invoicing work. It keeps customers, quotes, invoices, payments and repeat invoicing together, so you can spend less time jumping between records.

entries.question: Who is Tallyo for?
entries.answer: It works well for sole traders, freelancers, consultants, tradespeople and service companies that create quotes and invoices. Tallyo is built around the way your business works rather than one particular trade.

entries.question: What can I do with Tallyo?
entries.answer: You can create and email invoices, quotes and credit notes, save customers and items, personalise PDFs, track payments, schedule recurring invoices, choose overdue reminders and review document activity. You can also export your records and use account-protection controls. __TALLYO_CONNECT_PAYMENT_AVAILABILITY__

entries.question: How do I create an invoice or quote?
entries.answer: Start by choosing the document type, then add the customer, dates and products or services. Review the totals, save it and check the PDF; when everything looks right, you can email or download it.

links.label: Create invoices, quotes and credit notes

entries.question: What is the difference between a quote and an invoice?
triggers: difference between a quote and invoice
entries.answer: Think of a quote as the proposal you send before the customer agrees, while an invoice is the request for payment once the work is agreed or completed. When a customer accepts a quote, Tallyo can turn it into a linked invoice for you.

entries.question: What happens when a customer accepts a quote?
entries.answer: When your customer accepts, Tallyo keeps the original quote, records who accepted it and when, and creates one linked invoice. Nothing is lost—the accepted quote stays available alongside the new invoice.

entries.question: Can Tallyo send the invoice after a quote is accepted?
entries.answer: Yes, if automatic invoice email was selected before the quote was sent. You choose the due period and Tallyo uses the reviewed quote recipient. If automatic sending is off, or delivery fails, the linked invoice remains a Draft for you to review and send.

entries.question: What is a credit note?
triggers: when to use a credit note
entries.answer: A credit note lets you record a reduction to an invoice that has already been issued. The original invoice stays visible, and the adjustment is shown clearly rather than making the first document disappear.

entries.question: Can I save products and services?
entries.answer: Yes. Save products or services with their usual description and price, then reuse them on later documents. You can also create a new saved item while editing an invoice.

entries.question: Can I save customer details?
entries.answer: Yes—you can save a customer once and reuse their details on future documents. Their page also brings together balances, recent documents, recurring schedules and activity, without trying to become a full CRM.

entries.question: Can I import customers from a CSV file?
entries.answer: Yes. The Customers page reads the CSV locally, shows a preview and asks for confirmation before adding valid rows. It skips invalid rows and duplicate email addresses and does not overwrite existing customers.

entries.question: Can I add a percentage or fixed discount?
entries.answer: Yes. In the Tallyo app you can apply a percentage discount or enter a specific fixed amount, which is useful when you want the document total to reach an exact value.

entries.question: How do the tax modes work?
entries.answer: If the price you enter is before tax, choose Add tax on top. If tax is already included in that price, choose Prices include tax; Tallyo will then calculate and display the line and document totals to match.

entries.question: How do recurring invoices work?
entries.answer: You set how often the invoice should repeat, when the schedule starts and ends, and whether each new invoice is emailed automatically or left for you to review. If the work changes, you can pause or update the schedule.

entries.question: How do overdue reminders work?
entries.answer: An invoice becomes overdue when its due date has passed and there is still money to pay. You stay in control of reminders: Tallyo sends them only for the invoices where you turned them on, not for every overdue invoice automatically.

entries.question: How do I record a payment?
entries.answer: Open the invoice Payments section and add the amount, date and a short note for money received by bank transfer, cash or another agreed method. Tallyo updates the amount still left to pay.

entries.question: Can I record a deposit or part-payment?
entries.answer: Yes—you can add a deposit or part-payment to the invoice, and Tallyo will show what has been paid and what is still outstanding. Record the remaining amount later and the invoice will show as fully paid.

entries.question: How does Tallyo show what is paid and still due?
entries.answer: As you record deposits, part-payments and the final payment, each one stays with the invoice. You can quickly see the total paid, the balance left and whether the invoice is due, overdue or fully paid.

entries.question: Can customers pay by card?
triggers: how do stripe card payments work
entries.answer: __TALLYO_CONNECT_PAYMENT_FAQ__ You can also record payments received through another agreed route.

entries.question: Does Tallyo store card details?
entries.answer: Tallyo does not store payment-card details. When card payments are available for your account, Stripe hosts checkout and handles the card information.

entries.question: How do refunds work?
entries.answer: For a Stripe card payment confirmed in Tallyo, use the invoice refund action; Tallyo asks Stripe to process the refund and updates the invoice after signed confirmation. For payments received another way, refund through that route and keep the invoice record consistent.

entries.question: What does activity history show?
entries.answer: Activity history gives you a clear timeline of when a document was created or sent, when reminders went out and when payments were recorded. It is there to help with everyday follow-up, rather than act as a formal tamper-proof audit log.

entries.question: Can I check whether a document email was delivered?
entries.answer: Yes. Tallyo records the delivery result returned by the email service and shows it in the document activity. That helps you decide when to follow up, although a delivered message does not necessarily mean the customer has read it.

entries.question: Can I add my logo and brand colours?
entries.answer: Yes. In Branding you can add your logo, choose its position and select your brand colour while a live document preview shows the result. Tallyo keeps headings and totals readable even when the chosen colour is light.

links.label: See branding in the product tour

entries.question: Which invoice templates can I choose?
entries.answer: You can choose from four layouts: Tallyo, Basic, Modern and Professional. Open Branding, select the style you like and use the live preview to see how your details, items and totals will look.

entries.question: Can I turn alternating item colours off?
entries.answer: Yes. Branding includes a preference for alternating item-row colours. Leave it on for white and tinted rows, or turn it off for one consistent item background.

entries.question: Can I export my records?
entries.answer: Yes. Tallyo offers spreadsheet export for document lists and a structured account export for records associated with your account. Downloaded files are outside Tallyo's technical control, so store them appropriately.

entries.question: What can the Free Invoice Maker do?
entries.answer: You can make an invoice in your browser without creating an account. Add your business and customer details, items, discounts, tax, payment information and a logo, then preview, print or save the finished invoice as a PDF.

entries.question: What is not included in the Free Invoice Maker?
entries.answer: The free maker is designed for creating one document in your browser, so it does not save customers or services to an account. Email sending, document history, payment tracking, recurring invoices, reminders, cloud storage, credit notes and online payments are part of the full Tallyo workspace instead.

entries.question: Can I install Tallyo?
entries.answer: Yes. Open the Tallyo app by choosing Log in or Create account. On Chrome or Edge on a computer, look for the install or app symbol at the right end of the address bar. On Android Chrome use the three-dot menu. On iPhone or iPad Safari use the Page or Share menu, then Add to Home Screen.

entries.question: Can I use Tallyo on different devices?
entries.answer: Yes. Tallyo works in supported modern browsers on phone, tablet and computer and can be installed for quicker access. Authenticated business records still require an internet connection.

entries.question: Does Tallyo work offline?
entries.answer: Partly. The app shell can open offline, but you need an internet connection to sign in or view and update your business records. Recurring schedules and reminders also rely on Tallyo’s connected services.

entries.question: How do I create an account?
triggers: how do i create an account
entries.answer: Choose Create account on the Tallyo website, enter your details in the Tallyo app and complete the email-confirmation step.

entries.question: How do I log in?
entries.answer: Choose Log in on the Tallyo website to open the app. Use your confirmed account and complete authenticator verification when you have enabled it.

entries.question: How can I protect my Tallyo account?
entries.answer: Confirm your email, use a strong unique password and optionally add authenticator-app multi-factor authentication. Keep one-time recovery codes safely away from your usual device and use the all-devices sign-out option if access may be at risk.

entries.question: How much does Tallyo cost?
entries.answer: You can use the Free Invoice Maker for £0 without an account. Tallyo Pro is £8 per month or £80 per year for one business and one user. You can choose a monthly or annual subscription from Tallyo, whichever suits you best.

entries.question: Do monthly and annual plans have different features?
entries.answer: No—the features are the same on both options. Annual billing is £80 upfront and saves £16 compared with paying £8 each month for twelve months.

entries.question: Is there a free trial?
entries.answer: There is not currently a full-feature free trial. You can try the Free Invoice Maker without an account, or choose monthly billing if you want a lower-commitment way to explore the saved Tallyo workspace.

entries.question: What happens when I cancel Tallyo Pro?
entries.answer: When you cancel, future renewal stops but your paid access normally continues until the end of the billing period you have already paid for. Your records are not immediately deleted, and you can manage the cancellation through the Stripe Customer Portal in your Tallyo account.

entries.question: Does Tallyo Helper have private account access?
entries.answer: No—this Helper is only here to explain Tallyo’s public features. It cannot sign in to, inspect or change your account, and it cannot see private business records or provider information.

entries.question: What happens to a question I ask Tallyo Helper?
entries.answer: When the AI path is enabled, Tallyo sends only your current question and selected reviewed public guidance securely to OpenAI. Tallyo does not intentionally save the conversation, and the request uses store:false. Do not enter private business information or secrets.

entries.question: Does Tallyo replace accounting software?
entries.answer: No. Tallyo helps you manage invoicing and the records connected to it, but it is not a full accounting package. It does not prepare tax returns or provide legal, tax or accounting advice.

entries.question: How do I get support?
entries.answer: The quickest place to start is the Help Centre and its common questions. If you still need a hand, email main@tallyo.co.uk—but please never include passwords, authenticator or recovery codes, card details or bank information.

entries.question: Where can I read about security?
triggers: where can i read about security
entries.answer: You’ll find a clear overview on the Security page, including Tallyo’s account, data-access, payment and browser controls as well as their current limitations.
